claims.text: Powder mixtures of refractory high-entropy-alloy elements and Cu are prone to segregation because of high positive heats of mixing.
Spark plasma sintering provides rapid heating and controlled pressure.
Spark plasma sintering can promote an in-situ reaction between refractory elements and Cu.
A short dwell time at elevated temperature limits elemental segregation.
SPS produces fine-scale in-situ reaction layers.
The in-situ reaction layers produce a uniform dispersion of refractory phases in the Cu matrix.
The rapid kinetics of SPS reduce the time available for thermodynamically driven segregation.
Reduced segregation time stabilizes the microstructure during the reaction process.
SPS in-situ reactive synthesis can yield a large-scale refractory-alloy/Cu composite with a uniformly stable microstructure.
The resulting composite will contain well-mixed refractory and Cu phases.
The well-mixed phase structure will improve structural stability at high temperature.
The well-mixed phase structure will improve mechanical performance under high-temperature reactor conditions.
Conventional sintering or powder-metallurgy methods often cause phase segregation and unstable microstructures because of prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The effectiveness of SPS depends on alloy composition, temperature, pressure, and dwell time.
